issues.title: Some Armor Adds No Armor When Worn
issues.effect: Some armor pieces, such as Leather Pants and the Velosian Plume-helm, add no armor when worn and do not lower the damage you take, although their tooltips show an armor value.

steps.action: Take off all armor and open the character sheet.
steps.result: Armor shows 0.

steps.action: Hover Leather Pants in the inventory.
steps.result: The tooltip shows ARMOR: 4.

steps.action: Equip Leather Pants.
steps.result: Armor on the character sheet still shows 0.

issues.expected: Armor rises by the value the tooltip shows.
issues.observed: Armor on the character sheet stays at 0.
issues.cause: Equipping looks up the piece's row of ArmorDataTable by its English name without spaces and apostrophes. No row has that name, for example because the Velosian Plume-helm keeps its hyphen while its row is named VelosianPlumehelm, so the piece counts as Unarmored with no armor. Damage taken is multiplied by 1 minus the total armor divided by 100. The tooltip shows the item's ItemInfo.Damage instead, or the row whose armor name equals the item's name.

issues.title: Some Accessories Show Armor They Never Add
issues.effect: Some rings, amulets, belts, wings and packs, such as Bonecaller's Band and Pactborn Wings, show an armor value in their tooltips but add no armor when worn.

steps.action: Equip a piece of body armor that adds armor, such as a Cloth Hood, and open the character sheet.
steps.result: Armor rises. Note the new total.

steps.action: Hover Bonecaller's Band in the inventory.
steps.result: The tooltip shows ARMOR: 1.

steps.action: Equip Bonecaller's Band.
steps.result: Armor on the character sheet does not change.

issues.expected: Armor rises by the value the tooltip shows, or the tooltip shows no armor.
issues.observed: Armor on the character sheet stays the same.
issues.cause: The armor total adds up the head, torso, arms, legs, knee, feet and shoulder slots only. The tooltip shows the row of ArmorDataTable whose armor name equals the item's name, whatever slot the item is worn in.

issues.title: Trading Shows Less Damage for Some Assembled Weapons
issues.effect: Trading can show less damage than your inventory for the same assembled weapon. A grade D spear made from a Pine Polearm Shaft and Small Copper Spearhead shows three different values.

effectDetails.label: In Trading
effectDetails.text: The tooltip shows DAMAGE: 11.

effectDetails.label: In your inventory
effectDetails.text: The tooltip shows DAMAGE: 14.

effectDetails.label: On a hit
effectDetails.text: The spear deals 13.5 damage before modifiers.

issues.workaround: Check the tooltip in your inventory or equipment slot instead.

steps.action: At the anvil in Harbinger Stronghold, assemble a Spear with a Pine Polearm Shaft and a Small Copper Spearhead. If you finish with Quality: C, make another and finish with D.
steps.result: The spear is grade D. A grade C spear would show 15 damage on both screens.

steps.action: Open your character sheet and hover over the spear in your inventory.
steps.result: The tooltip shows DAMAGE: 14.

steps.action: Close the character sheet and speak to Theo Macgowan in Harbinger Stronghold. Choose "Let's see what you have in stock."
steps.result: The Trading window opens.

steps.action: Hover over the spear under Your Inventory in Trading.
steps.result: The tooltip shows DAMAGE: 11.

issues.expected: Trading and the character sheet agree on the damage of the same weapon.
issues.observed: Theo's normally opened Trading window built a tooltip with DAMAGE: 11 for the grade D spear. Its inventory and equipment tooltips showed DAMAGE: 14. An ordinary hit removed 13.5 health from an unarmored target. To capture the Trading tooltip in the lab, the existing tooltip widget was moved from its holder into the viewport without changing its text or visibility.
issues.cause: Assembly scales and truncates the stored part damage. Trading reads that stored number. The equipped weapon recomputes damage from its parts with a different multiplier for grades D and F. The character sheet rounds the recomputed value, which can also differ from the stored number when the multipliers agree.

issues.title: Equipping Knee Guards Does Not Update Armor
issues.effect: Putting on or swapping knee guards leaves Armor on the character sheet unchanged. Putting on or taking off another piece of armor afterward makes the guards' armor count.

/Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Armo.effect: Equipping Broad Knee Guards leaves Armor unchanged, although the tooltip shows ARMOR: 7.
/Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Armo.workaround: After equipping the guards, put on or take off another piece of armor, such as a Cloth Hood.

/Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Armo.effect: Equipping Standard Cap Guards leaves Armor unchanged, although the tooltip shows ARMOR: 6.
/Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Armo.workaround: After equipping the guards, put on or take off another piece of armor, such as a Cloth Hood.

issues.workaround: After equipping the guards, put on or take off another piece of armor, such as a Cloth Hood.

steps.action: Close any tutorial pop-ups. Open the character sheet and take off all armor.
steps.result: Armor shows 0.

steps.action: Equip Broad Knee Guards.
steps.result: Their tooltip shows ARMOR: 7, but Armor stays at 0.

steps.action: Put on another piece of armor, such as a Cloth Hood.
steps.result: Armor updates to count the guards. With a Cloth Hood, it rises to 10.

steps.action: Take off the Cloth Hood.
steps.result: Armor drops to 7. The guards' armor still counts.

issues.expected: Armor shows 7 once the knee guards are equipped.
issues.observed: In issue-knees-short-1125 and issue-knees-armed-1125, Armor stayed at 0 after equipping the guards alone or with a sword. Adding a Cloth Hood raised it to 10 with Broad Knee Guards or 9 with Standard Cap Guards. Swapping guards alone left the old total in place. In design-facts (2026-11-25T20-49-18-980Z), Armor stayed at 3 when Broad Knee Guards went on after a Cloth Hood. Removing and replacing the hood gave 7 and 10. Equipping the guards alone left Armor at 0, and adding Leather Pants raised it to 7.
issues.cause: The knee branch of Attach Equipment does not call Set player Speed based on Armor, so it skips Retrieve Player Armor and leaves the previous total in place. Equipping a helmet runs that recalculation after a Delay. A pausing tutorial can prevent that delay from completing until gameplay resumes.

issues.title: Foragers Feast Gives a Flower Instead of a Meal
issues.effect: Cooking Foragers Feast uses Chicken Meat and two Love-me-not Flowers but gives back only one Love-me-not Flower.

/Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Craf.effect: Cooking Foragers Feast gives a Love-me-not Flower instead of a meal.

steps.action: At a cooking fire, add one Chicken Meat and two Love-me-not Flowers to the pot.
steps.result: The pot contains all three ingredients.

steps.action: Choose "Cook!" and wait for it to finish.
steps.result: The result shows a flower. If this is your first time cooking the recipe, the game shows "Recipe Discovered!"

steps.action: Check your inventory.
steps.result: The ingredients are used up, and you get back one Love-me-not Flower instead of a meal.

issues.expected: Cooking Foragers Feast gives a meal.
issues.observed: With two flowers the game discovers Foragers Feast, awards 25 Cooking EXP, consumes the ingredients and gives one Love-me-not Flower. With only one flower the game instead rejects the ingredients as an invalid recipe and returns them.
issues.cause: Check Data Table for Recipe matches the ingredients against the ForagersFeast row in ItemRecipes, which requires two flowers. Translate Data Table Row to Item Class then reads the output from AllFoodRecipes, whose ForagersFeast row points to Love-me-not Flower.
citations: /Game/BloodlinesAlpha/UI/CookingWindow:Translate Data Table Row to Item Class

steps.action: Lose some health and hover Steak in the inventory.
steps.result: The description says it restores 80 health.

steps.action: Eat the Steak.
steps.result: The Steak is gone, and Health keeps regenerating as before.

issues.expected: Health rises by 80.
issues.observed: The food is used up, and Health does not rise beyond its normal regeneration.
issues.cause: Eating looks up the food's row of FoodEffectDataTable by its name without spaces and apostrophes, and then by its localized name. No row matches these foods, so eating applies no effect.

issues.title: Druid's Stew Does Not Boost Foraging Experience
issues.effect: Druid's Stew grants Druidsight but not the foraging experience boost it lists.

/Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Craf.effect: Despite its description, Druid's Stew does not boost foraging experience. It still gives Druidsight.

steps.action: Eat Druid's Stew.
steps.result: The status effects show Druidsight but no foraging experience boost.

steps.action: Eat Carrot Cake.
steps.result: The foraging experience boost appears.

issues.title: Some Foods Restore Different Amounts than Their Descriptions Say

effectDetails.label: Health and mana amounts reversed
effectDetails.text: Buttered Bread restores 15 health and 30 mana, not 30 health and 15 mana.

effectDetails.label: Health instead of stamina
effectDetails.text: Spud Colossus restores up to 200 health and no stamina. Its description says 200 stamina.

/Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Craf.effect: Despite its description, Buttered Bread restores 15 health and 30 mana when eaten.
Despite its description, Spud Colossus restores 200 health and no stamina when eaten.

steps.action: Lose some health and mana. Hover Buttered Bread in the inventory.
steps.result: The description says it restores 30 health and 15 mana.

steps.action: Eat the Buttered Bread.
steps.result: Health rises by 15 and Mana by 30, up to their maximums.

steps.action: Lose some health and stamina, then hover Spud Colossus in the inventory.
steps.result: The description says it restores 200 stamina.

steps.action: Eat the Spud Colossus.
steps.result: Health rises by up to 200, and Stamina keeps regenerating as before.

issues.expected: Buttered Bread restores 30 health and 15 mana, and Spud Colossus restores 200 stamina.
issues.observed: Buttered Bread restores 15 health and 30 mana. Spud Colossus restores 200 health, up to the maximum, and no stamina.

issues.title: Some Potions Do Nothing or Have the Wrong Effect

effectDetails.label: No effect
effectDetails.text: Health Potion, Mana Potion and Castleside Cider.

effectDetails.label: Stamina only
effectDetails.text: Dwarfs Flaggon restores 60 stamina.

/Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Heal.effect: Health Potion has no description in its inventory tooltip and restores no health, mana or stamina.

/Game/ManaPotion.ManaPotion_C.effect: Mana Potion has no description in its inventory tooltip and restores no health, mana or stamina.

/Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Cast.effect: Castleside Cider is consumed without restoring health, mana or stamina.

/Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/TheD.effect: Dwarfs Flaggon restores 60 stamina without restoring health or mana.

steps.action: Lose some health, mana and stamina. Hover Health Potion and Mana Potion in your inventory.
steps.result: Neither tooltip has a description.

steps.action: Use Health Potion.
steps.result: The potion is consumed. Health, Mana and Stamina regenerate as before.

steps.action: Use Mana Potion.
steps.result: The potion is consumed. Health, Mana and Stamina regenerate as before.

steps.action: Use Castleside Cider.
steps.result: The cider is consumed. Health, Mana and Stamina regenerate as before.

steps.action: Use Dwarfs Flaggon with at least 60 stamina missing.
steps.result: Stamina rises by 60 at once. Health and Mana regenerate as before.

issues.expected: Using the potions applies their configured effects. The Dwarfs Flaggon hot-swap tooltip lists Drunk for 60 seconds.
issues.observed: Health Potion, Mana Potion and Castleside Cider are used up without restoring health, mana or stamina. Castleside Cider shows no status. Dwarfs Flaggon restores 60 stamina and does not change health or mana beyond natural regeneration. Its status list stayed empty after drinking. Its inventory tooltip omits the description that Trading and hot-swap show.
issues.cause: Using a potion runs FoodManager's Drink Potion, which reads each effect slot's power as an effect number of PotionEffectTranslatorTable and its duration as the amount, as the potion crafting window writes potions. These potions store their real powers there, such as 345 for Restore Health, which are no effect numbers. Dwarfs Flaggon's Improved Jumping holds 5, the number of Restore Stamina, with 60 as its duration.

issues.title: Some Staves Launch No Fireballs
issues.effect: Despite their descriptions, Fairy Staff, Gripclaw Staff and the two staves named Soulstaff launch no fireballs and use no mana.

/Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Weap.effect: Despite its description, Fairy Staff launches no fireballs and uses no mana.
Despite its description, Gripclaw Staff launches no fireballs and uses no mana.
Despite its description, Soulstaff launches no fireballs, uses no mana and deals no damage.
Despite its description, Soulstaff launches no fireballs, uses no mana and deals no damage.

steps.action: Hover Fairy Staff in the inventory.
steps.result: Its description says each swing launches small fireballs and consumes 5 mana.

steps.action: Equip and draw Fairy Staff with at least 5 mana available.
steps.result: The staff is visible in hand.

steps.action: Use normal attacks while aiming into open space.
steps.result: The staff swings, but no fireball appears and the mana bar does not drop.

steps.action: Repeat with Gripclaw Staff or a staff named Soulstaff.
steps.result: They show the same description, and their swings launch no fireball either.

issues.expected: Each normal swing launches a small fireball and consumes 5 mana, as the description says.
issues.observed: Normal swings of Fairy Staff, Gripclaw Staff and both staves named Soulstaff create no projectile and consume no mana. Fairy Staff's charged attacks, blocking and attacks while blocking also produced no fireball in either first-person or third-person view.
issues.cause: The inventory tooltip displays each staff's ItemInfo.Description. Fairy Staff, Gripclaw Staff and both Soulstaff classes have the same description as Staff of Minor Flames, whose Swing Event spends 5 mana and spawns a fireball. Their own Swing Events spawn no projectile and spend no mana.

issues.title: Some Staves Deal 100 Damage at Close Range

effectDetails.label: Hits as the projectile leaves the staff
effectDetails.text: Walking Stick, Acolyte Geomancer Staff and Moonstone Staff can deal 100 damage. Attacking at close range can make this happen.

effectDetails.label: Hits after the projectile travels
effectDetails.text: Walking Stick deals 12 damage, Acolyte Geomancer Staff deals 20 and Moonstone Staff deals 35.

/Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Weap.effect: Walking Stick's projectile deals 100 damage instead of 12 if it hits an enemy as it leaves the staff. Attacking from close range can make this happen.
Acolyte Geomancer Staff's projectile deals 100 damage instead of 20 if it hits an enemy as it leaves the staff. Attacking from close range can make this happen.
Moonstone Staff's projectile deals 100 damage instead of 35 if it hits an enemy as it leaves the staff. Attacking from close range can make this happen.

steps.action: Equip and draw Acolyte Geomancer Staff with enough mana to attack and no damage-changing effects active.
steps.result: The staff is visible in hand.

steps.action: Attack a goblin from far enough away for the projectile to travel before impact.
steps.result: A normal projectile hit shows 20 damage.

steps.action: Face a goblin at close melee range and use normal attacks through the second swing of the combo.
steps.result: A projectile that hits as it appears can show 100 damage.

steps.action: Repeat with Walking Stick and Moonstone Staff.
steps.result: Their distant projectile hits show 12 and 35 damage respectively. Hits as the projectile leaves the staff can show 100.

issues.expected: Normal projectile hits use the same base damage at both ranges: 12 for Walking Stick, 20 for Acolyte Geomancer Staff and 35 for Moonstone Staff.
issues.observed: All three staves dealt 100 projectile damage when the projectile overlapped the goblin during creation. At longer range, Walking Stick dealt 12, Acolyte Geomancer Staff dealt 20 and Moonstone Staff dealt 35.
issues.cause: GenericStaffProjectile starts with Damage 100. These three staves call FinishSpawningActor before assigning their literal projectile Damage values of 12, 20 and 35. If the projectile overlaps an enemy during that call, the overlap applies the default 100 before the staff writes its normal value. Whether this happens depends on the projectile's spawn position and the enemy's collision, not a fixed distance.

issues.title: Some Weapons Deal Different Damage than Their Tooltips Show

effectDetails.label: Melee weapons
effectDetails.text: Daggers, spears and some swords deal less or more damage than their tooltips show.

effectDetails.label: Ranged weapons
effectDetails.text: Guns, pistols and bows show different damage than a single body hit deals.

effectDetails.label: Shields
effectDetails.text: Their tooltips show damage that shields never deal with a normal attack.

effectDetails.label: Staves
effectDetails.text: Some show different damage than their projectiles deal.

steps.action: Hover Goblin Shiv in the inventory, then equip it and hit an enemy without damage-changing effects.
steps.result: The tooltip shows Damage: 20, but the hit deals 8 damage.

steps.action: Repeat with Farmer's Pitchfork and Bloodforged Blade.
steps.result: The tooltip numbers are 35 and 55, while the hits deal 10 and 35.

steps.action: Hover Copper Flintlock Pistol, then shoot an enemy's body and head from several steps away.
steps.result: The tooltip shows Damage: 100. A body hit deals 50 damage and a headshot deals 100.

steps.action: Repeat with another affected gun or bow. Compare a single projectile's body hit with the tooltip, not the whole shot.
steps.result: The tooltip number differs from the body hit.

steps.action: Hover Areman Shield, then equip it with no weapon and try a normal attack.
steps.result: The tooltip shows Damage: 15, but the attack deals no damage.

steps.action: Hover Walking Stick, then hit an enemy from a few steps away so its projectile travels before impact.
steps.result: The tooltip shows Damage: 2, but the hit deals 12 damage. Pinto Staff, Fairy Staff and Gripclaw Staff hit with their swings for 10 instead.

issues.expected: A weapon's Damage tooltip describes the damage its normal hit applies.
issues.observed: Goblin Shiv dealt 8 damage, Farmer's Pitchfork 10 and Bloodforged Blade 35, against tooltip values of 20, 35 and 55. Copper Flintlock Pistol dealt 50 on a body hit and 100 on a headshot, against tooltip Damage 100. Powerful Blunderbuss pellets dealt 0 on a body hit and 20 on a headshot, against tooltip Damage 300. Attacking with only Areman Shield or Lonland Shield dealt no damage, despite tooltip Damage 15 and 100. Walking Stick, Adept Cryomancer Staff, Moonstone Staff and Winter's Whisper dealt 12, 20, 35 and 35 from range, while Pinto Staff, Fairy Staff and Gripclaw Staff dealt 10 with their swings.
issues.cause: The tooltip shows ItemInfo.Damage. Melee hits use WeaponInfo.Damage, while ranged hits use projectile damage and can add a separate headshot bonus. Some staves assign their projectile's damage in Staff Attack instead. A shield has no ordinary attack that applies damage, so its tooltip number describes no normal hit. Shield Charge damage is separate. The affected weapons' ItemInfo.Damage differs from what these paths apply.

issues.title: Some Weapons Train No Weapon Proficiency
issues.effect: Hits with these weapons add no EXP to One-Handed Weapons, Two-Handed Weapons or any other passive level.

steps.action: On a new character, open the character sheet and choose Detailed Stats.
steps.result: Under Passive Levels, One-Handed Weapons and Two-Handed Weapons show 0/50 EXP.

steps.action: Equip and draw Lonland Halberd, hit an enemy once and open Detailed Stats again.
steps.result: No passive level shows more EXP.

steps.action: Hit an enemy once with Bloodforged Blade and open Detailed Stats again.
steps.result: One-Handed Weapons shows 2/50 EXP.

issues.expected: Each hit adds EXP to a passive level, as hits with other melee weapons do.
issues.observed: Hits with Lonland Halberd, Standard Greataxe, Fairy Staff and each other affected weapon add no EXP to any passive level. A hit with Bloodforged Blade adds 2 EXP to One-Handed Weapons, a hit with Copper Battleaxe 2 EXP to Two-Handed Weapons, and hits with staves such as Moonstone Staff add EXP to Focuses.
issues.cause: A melee hit passes the weapon's WeaponInfo.AttackType to Add Proper Weapon EXP. One-handed, dagger, spear and two-handed attacks each add EXP to their passive level. A halberd attack adds Staff EXP, which Detailed Stats shows as [Focuses](discipline:focuses), only when the weapon's Weapon Class is Staff, and nothing for any other class. Copper Battleaxe swings like a halberd but passes the two-handed attack type, so it trains Two-Handed Weapons.

issues.observed: In 29 of 31 groups of placed items that share a save tag, taking one made the others disappear about a minute after the area loaded again, as did taking one of the five items without a tag. Taking both items of a pair in one visit kept both.
issues.cause: Taking an item adds its Tag to the game instance's Completed Achievements, and an item whose Tag is listed destroys itself when its area loads. Each pair shares one Tag, and the five items carry none, so they share the Tag None.

issues.title: Blood Magic Points Follow the Blood Setting
issues.effect: Each time [Blood Magic](discipline:blood-magic) levels up, your [Blood Levels](mechanic:blood-levels) setting determines how many Blood Magic points you get. They replace the points you had, so points you saved are lost.

effectDetails.label: No blood
effectDetails.text: 2 points.

effectDetails.label: A bit of blood
effectDetails.text: 3 points.

effectDetails.label: Default Amount
effectDetails.text: 4 points.

effectDetails.label: BLOODBATH
effectDetails.text: 6 points.

/Game/UltimateSkillSystem/SkillsData/Blo.effect: Each time Blood Magic levels up, your Blood Magic points are set to 2, 3, 4 or 6, depending on your [Blood Levels](mechanic:blood-levels) setting. Points you saved are lost.
/Game/UltimateSkillSystem/SkillsData/Blo.workaround: Set Blood Levels to BLOODBATH in the pause menu under Settings, Video and Effect Settings before Blood Magic levels up, and spend your points before its next level.

issues.workaround: Set Blood Levels to BLOODBATH in the pause menu under Settings, Video and Effect Settings before Blood Magic levels up, and spend your points before its next level.

steps.action: Open Settings from the pause menu, choose Video and Effect Settings and set Blood Levels to No blood.
steps.result: Blood Levels shows No blood.

steps.action: Gain a Blood Magic level and open the Blood Magic skill tree.
steps.result: Blood Magic Proficiency Points shows 2.

steps.action: Set Blood Levels to BLOODBATH and gain another Blood Magic level.
steps.result: The tree shows 6 points.

steps.action: Spend points on a passive and gain another Blood Magic level.
steps.result: The tree shows 6 points again.

issues.expected: Each Blood Magic level adds Blood Magic points to the ones you have, as levels of other disciplines do.
issues.observed: After a Blood Magic level the tree shows the Blood Levels setting plus one: 2 with No blood, 3 with A bit of blood, 4 with Default Amount and 6 with BLOODBATH. After spending 2 of 3 points, the next level restored 3.
issues.cause: The game's function Add Proficiency Points sets Bloodmagic Points to the game instance's Blood Level plus one instead of adding to them. Blood Level holds the Blood Levels option of the video settings window, which its Blood selection writes and enemies read when they bleed.

issues.title: Rusty Crossbows from Merchants and Squalls End Fire Nothing
issues.effect: The Rusty Crossbow sold by merchants or found lying in Squalls End fires no bolt and deals no damage.

effectDetails.label: Elderglen
effectDetails.text: The Rusty Crossbow the shopkeeper sells.

effectDetails.label: Squalls End
effectDetails.text: The Rusty Crossbow the shopkeeper sells and the one lying in the area.

issues.workaround: Choose Crossbow when Geoffrey Woodkin offers you a ranged weapon in Harbinger Stronghold. The Rusty Crossbow he gives works. A crate at Parford Lake sometimes holds one too.

steps.action: Buy a Rusty Crossbow from the shopkeeper in Squalls End and keep arrows in your inventory.
steps.result: Your inventory holds the crossbow and the arrows.

steps.action: Equip and draw it.
steps.result: The crossbow is in your hands.

steps.action: Fire at an enemy.
steps.result: No bolt leaves the crossbow, and the enemy's health stays the same.

issues.expected: Firing shoots a bolt that hits for the crossbow's damage.
issues.observed: Ten shots at 100 to 600 units fired no bolt and took no health from a Goblin Brute. The shopkeepers of Squalls End and Elderglen stock this crossbow. The other Rusty Crossbow, which crates and Geoffrey Woodkin give, hit the same Goblin Brute for 85. In run geoffrey1, Geoffrey Woodkin in Harbinger Stronghold used the dialogue whose Crossbow choice gives it.
issues.cause: Merchants and the placed crossbow in Squalls End give the class RustyCrossbow, which derives from BP_BasicSword rather than Crossbow, so it has none of Crossbow's firing functions. The Rusty Crossbow that crates and Geoffrey Woodkin give is Rusty_Crossbow, which derives from Crossbow.

issues.title: Some Spells Ignore Their Damage Passives
issues.effect: Spire Barrage, Earth Hammer, Earth Spikes, Inferno Lance, Emberspark, Emberspike and Spark deal the same damage at every rank of their discipline's damage passives, although those passives promise more damage for the whole discipline.

/Game/UltimateSkillSystem/SkillSystemSki.effect: Cryomancy's damage passives do not raise Spire Barrage's damage. Each spear deals 30 at every rank.

/Game/Skill_EarthHammer.Skill_EarthHamme.effect: Geomancy's damage passives do not raise Earth Hammer's damage. Its hits deal 25 and 100 at every rank.

/Game/UltimateSkillSystem/SkillSystemSki.effect: Pyromancy's damage passives do not raise Inferno Lance's damage. Its lance deals 150 and its explosion 50 at every rank.

/Game/UltimateSkillSystem/SystemDemonstr.effect: Pyromancy's damage passives do not raise Emberspark's damage. Its hit deals 25 at every rank.

/Game/UltimateSkillSystem/SkillSystemSki.effect: Geomancy's damage passives do not raise Earth Spikes' damage. Its hit deals 100 at every rank.
Pyromancy's damage passives do not raise Emberspike's damage. Its hit deals 100 at every rank.

/Game/UltimateSkillSystem/SystemDemonstr.effect: Electromancy's damage passives do not raise Spark's damage. Its hit deals 15 at every rank.

steps.action: Before buying any Cryomancy damage passive, such as Frostbite, cast Ice Shard and Spire Barrage at an enemy.
steps.result: Ice Shard deals 25 damage, and each spear of Spire Barrage deals 30.

steps.action: Buy all 5 ranks of Frostbite, whose description says "+2% cryomancy damage per rank", and cast both again.
steps.result: Ice Shard deals 27.5 damage. Each spear of Spire Barrage still deals 30.

issues.expected: Every rank of a discipline's damage passives raises the damage of these spells, as it does for the discipline's other spells.
issues.observed: With all five damage passives of their discipline at rank 0 and at their highest rank, Spire Barrage's spears dealt 30, Earth Hammer's hits 25 and 100, Earth Spikes' hit 100, Inferno Lance's lance 150 and its explosion 50, Emberspark's hit 25, Emberspike's hit 100 and Spark's hit 15. Each skill was cast in a freshly opened level. In the same run Ice Shard rose from 25 to 43.75, and 53 other spells rose by the same 75%.
issues.cause: Each discipline's damage passives are added up by one function, and a spell multiplies its damage by the result. These seven spells hit with fixed numbers instead of that product.

steps.action: Note your gold. In Woodhurst, ask Mysha Bullock "What do you have to eat?" and reply "Just some chicken, please."
steps.result: She says "That'll be 150 gold."

steps.action: Reply "Here you go."
steps.result: You get one Chicken Meat, and your gold drops by 15.

issues.expected: The seller takes the gold they name.
issues.observed: Every order of the two waitresses was bought once. In Woodhurst Mysha Bullock named 250, 150, 150, 50 and 50 gold for Honey Glazed Ham, Chicken Meat, Steak, Rum and Ale and took 10, 15, 7, 10 and 10. Castleside Cider cost the 120 she named. In Harbingers Arena Heidi Blanchard, whom the dialogue window also calls Mysha Bullock, named 10 for Steak and took 7, named 5 for Turkey Leg and took 6, and took what she named for Soup, Rum, Ale and Dwarfs Flaggon. With the quest Dependence Substitution active, accepting Silent Wyn's offer of 250 gold gave one Dewdrop and left gold at 750.
issues.cause: A waitress's order takes the item's value, such as 7 for Steak, whatever her line says. Silent Wyn's conversation has no step that takes gold.
